text: For in-network medical care, the provider generally submits the claim. For out-of-network care, either the provider or member may need to submit it, and a member filing directly uses the Member Claim Submission Form.

source.title: How to file a claim for your GEHA health plan

text: GEHA directs members to official claim, appeal, reimbursement, privacy, and authorization forms in its Forms and Documents resource center. The applicable form depends on medical, dental, vision, prescription, reimbursement, or appeal workflow.

GEHA identifies claim denials, adverse benefit determinations, and prior-authorization decisions as appealable. Its published process begins with an initial appeal, may proceed to reconsideration, and may then allow OPM review when applicable.

source.title: GEHA Appeal Process and Disputed Claims FAQs

text: A GEHA appeal submission should identify the member and plan, date of service, claim control number, billed amount, provider, and the basis of the dispute. Time limits and the correct secure filing channel must be verified for the specific case.

source.title: GEHA Appeal Process and Disputed Claims FAQs

text: OPM expects FEHB carriers to explain disputed-claim processes for pre-service, post-service, and pharmacy claims, including deadlines, access to relevant materials, reconsideration, OPM review, forms, and secure submission methods.
GEHA requires prior authorization before some services and procedures. Providers use the provider portal for submission and assistance; members use the MyGEHA member portal for information and help.

Systems handling electronic protected health information require risk-based safeguards, including authorized access, audit controls, integrity protections, identity authentication, and transmission security.

source.title: HHS Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule
